hypothesis: If a_v186 admits crops, animals, land, and discretionary work only when their forecast survival, harvest, travel, deposit, and sale demand fits inside conservative worker capacity, then missed service, expiry, overflow, and terminally stranded value will fall enough to improve terminal win probability, especially in days 15-29 and labor-heavy opponent strata.

exact_code_lever.change: Insert admit_project(project, state, horizon=48) before BUY_SEED, BUY_ANIMAL, BUY_LAND, BUILD, and PLANT jobs. Replace the open_jobs/JOBS_PER_UNIT workforce heuristic with a demand-bound table of jobs carrying release, deadline, service_actions, travel_lower_bound, required_item, value, and abandonment class.
exact_code_lever.gate: Admit only when, for every deadline boundary t in the next 48 turns, p90 mandatory demand(t)+candidate recurring demand(t)+return reserve(t) <= 0.80*available worker-turns(t), minimum slack remains >=4 turns, projected shed peak <=90, cash reserve remains nonnegative, and all production can be sold before step 719.
exact_code_lever.load_shed_order: When infeasible, reject new development first, then CARE, FERTILIZE, low-price COLLECT_FERTILIZER, non-expiring low-value HARVEST, DIG, and optional WATER; never shed a second-consecutive WATER/FEED, an expiring valuable harvest, return-to-shed, or terminal sell.

affected_phase: Active on every planning call, strongest after land expansion, animal placement, days 15-20 service congestion, any hour >=12 with unfinished mandatory jobs, shed load >=80, and the terminal horizon. Opponent strata with aggressive supply or hiring alter value but never relax survival feasibility.
engine_mechanism: Each farmer/hand has one field action per turn; hands hired during market processing cannot recover the current turn and disappear at end of day. Plants and animals fail after two consecutive missed end-of-day refreshes, so survival jobs have hard deadlines. Water can create crop yield only in defined windows; feed gates animal production and survival. Harvest creates carried cargo that must reach the four shed-access tiles, be deposited, then sold through capped market orders. Shed overflow is destroyed. Locked tiles are traversable but tile actions are no-ops. New projects create recurring service and travel demand, not just purchase cost.
regime_trigger_and_forecast_error: Recompute admission after every plant/animal/weed/land/shop change and at hours 0, 6, 12, and 18. Forecast mandatory releases over 48 turns from exact lifecycle state; use a 90th-percentile travel multiplier learned by phase and route density. Log predicted versus realized service actions, travel, new weeds, harvest volume, shed peak, and price. Tighten utilization from 0.80 to 0.70 when realized demand exceeds forecast by >15% twice in one day; relax by 0.05 after three accurate days, never above 0.85 [uncertain].
decision_score_audit: Each project and job logs gross value, terminal feasibility, action count, travel bound, deadlines, demand-bound contribution at each boundary, capacity, minimum slack, cash/shed/order constraints, normalized net value per worker-turn, admit/reject decision, rejection reason, and gap to feasibility. Reasons include survival overload, harvest overload, travel overload, cash reserve, shed peak, terminal maturity, market slot, and negative net value.
admissible_workload_and_minimum_slack: For each future boundary t, compute demand from released jobs whose deadline <=t plus a lower bound on route transitions and shed returns. Capacity is sum over active units of usable turns before t, excluding the current market-hire turn, end-of-day reset, and reserved terminal moves. Existing threatened service is mandatory; candidate projects add daily WATER or FEED/CARE/collect/harvest plus wheat/fertilizer pickup. Gate at p90 utilization <=0.80 and minimum latest-start slack >=4 turns; require >=8-turn slack for projects crossing a day boundary [uncertain].
constraint_utilization_profile: Telemetry by day: worker-action utilization, mandatory utilization, movement share, money reserve utilization, occupied/unlocked tiles, shed peak/100, mean cargo/worker, and market orders/10. Red bands: mandatory labor >80%, movement >45%, shed >90%, cash after committed inputs < next-day survival bill, or market orders >8. New land is rejected if its extra route and weed exposure raise any red constraint.
job_queue_health: Track queue count/value by WATER, FEED, HARVEST, CARE, FERTILIZE, COLLECT, DIG, PICKUP, DROP, BUILD, and PLANT; age, deadline, slack, lateness, starvation, invalidation, and abandonment. Service queues use earliest-deadline-first within feasibility class; overloaded optional work is abandoned immediately rather than aging behind survival work. Zero late survival jobs is a hard guardrail.
spatial_logistics_metrics: Estimate project travel from worker-to-tile assignment plus minimum spanning route increments and mandatory shed returns. Record distance/completed job, empty travel, route switches, jobs per excursion, harvest batch size, wheat/fertilizer pickup batch, and shed trips. Admission uses the larger of geometric lower bound and phase-specific p90 realized travel, preventing remote land from appearing free.
expected_terminal_value: Expected benefit is avoided lost assets, recovered harvest, lower overflow, and fewer wasted purchases minus foregone gross production. The candidate has not been implemented or benchmarked; incremental terminal cash and win uplift remain [uncertain].
marginal_value_per_worker_turn: For an admitted project, divide discounted terminal sale value minus inputs, market impact, expected missed-work loss, and overflow risk by incremental service+travel+deposit actions. Reject below the current marginal value of reserved capacity. Empirical thresholds and uplift are [uncertain].
shadow_price_vector: Use phase-specific finite differences: lambda_labor=max net value of the best rejected feasible job per action; lambda_move=lambda_labor times expected displacement penalty; lambda_money=terminal value lost by withholding one coin from committed inputs; lambda_tile=best rejected project value per tile-day; lambda_shed=overflow-risk value per peak slot; lambda_order=best displaced market order; lambda_cargo=extra return/overflow cost. Initial numerical values require calibration [uncertain].
gross_to_net_value_decomposition: For every project: gross forecast sale revenue minus seed/animal/structure/feed/fertilizer cost, hire cost, service labor shadow cost, travel shadow cost, tile occupancy, shed/cargo/order costs, expected price impact, expiry/escape probability, overflow, financing delay, and displaced projects. Store realized decomposition and an exact residual to terminal cash.
market_and_opponent_dependence: Opponent production and town demand change sale value and price-impact loss but not service demand. Under premium glut, shed or abandon optional low-value harvest before survival work and stop admitting long premium projects. Under high absorption, admit only if workload remains feasible. Wheat price and supply enter the full animal feed commitment, not one-day cost.
action_validity_and_noop_breakdown: Admission must eliminate jobs known to be impossible: already serviced, target removed, locked action tile, missing input, full shed, insufficient cash, duplicate contention, expired lifecycle, wrong structure, or terminally unsellable cargo. Instrument attempted/valid/executed/no-op by reason. Baseline crop-service logic already suppresses some at-cap/doomed work, but complete realized no-op results are [uncertain].
micro_scenario_coverage: Deterministic tests: one plant at consecutive_unwatered=1 near day end; animal unfed with no wheat; two workers contending for one seed/input; remote harvest with exact return slack; new animal causing next-day overload; land expansion with distant jobs; shed at 99/100; ten market orders; expiring crop decay; crop maturing after terminal; hand hired at hour 23; overloaded queue load shedding; and price collapse after admission.
terminal_feasibility: Every cargo-producing job must reserve HARVEST/COLLECT + route-to-shed + DROP/end-of-day capacity + one SELL order before step 719. Stop new planting when maturity plus p90 service/return/sale exceeds remaining turns. At or beyond the last feasible start, shed optional work, harvest only bankable value, route all carriers home, then liquidate; unsold inventory has zero terminal value.
paired_test_design: Control a_v186.py versus a single candidate with only the admission/load-shedding lever, same opponent/seed/seat blocks. Use the confirmatory 1,536-pair stratified design; oversample labor-heavy, remote-expansion, and glut opponents in tuning but retain equal-stratum confirmation. Primary metric is paired terminal-win uplift; secondary metrics are late survival jobs, overflow, abandoned value, and terminal cash.
paired_discordance_and_effect_interval: Report control-only and candidate-only wins, paired uplift and 95% cluster interval. Plan for +5 points; with 1,536 pairs the approximate 80%-power MDE is 3.2-5.0 points as discordance ranges .20-.50. Actual discordance and effect interval are [uncertain].
random_stream_alignment: Use event-keyed exogenous draws or audit semantic RNG alignment. This lever deliberately changes occupancy and therefore the official conditional weed RNG stream will diverge under equal seeds; uninstrumented same-seed runs must be analyzed as seed-blocked clusters, not assumed perfect common random numbers.
optional_stopping_and_multiple_testing_b: Freeze utilization cap, horizon, slack, and load-shed order before confirmation. Screen at most four variants (cap 0.70/0.80 and horizon 24/48) on tuning data; use Holm correction if more than one reaches shared validation. No outcome-driven early stopping; use a time-uniform confidence sequence only if monitoring is unavoidable.
tuning_validation_separation: Fit travel percentiles and forecast-error bands on tuning opponents/seeds. Freeze them before validation. Use disjoint opponent hashes and seed namespaces for validation and final confirmation. Limit to four explicit tuning variants and retain a_v186 behavior as the timeout fallback.
distributional_guardrails: Require zero increase in animal escapes and weeds caused by missed survival, overflow rate not worse, 10th-percentile cash delta nonnegative within -2,000 tolerance, catastrophic-loss rate not up >1 point, and no seat or opponent-stratum win loss >3 points. Results are [uncertain].
robustness_regret: Measure regret against the best workload cap/horizon per opponent stratum and against a_v186 in the worst stratum. Prefer a slightly conservative cap if its worst-stratum regret is lower even when mean cash is lower. No results yet [uncertain].
rare_event_stress_results: Stress dense weeds, day-0 liquidity squeeze, wheat-price spike, duplicated premium shops absent, sudden glut, 95% shed occupancy, hour-18 worker loss equivalent, remote SE land, and several simultaneous expiry deadlines. Expected direction is fewer deadline misses; measured results are [uncertain].
interaction_and_ablation_matrix: Ablate admission gate, p90 travel, shed constraint, cash/feed reserve, terminal chain, and load-shed priority. Pairwise tests with rolling-horizon planning, regime triggers, hiring reservation, and shadow-price scoring must show whether each adds benefit beyond the common workload model. Interactions are [uncertain].
promotion_margin_and_reversion_trigger: Promote if paired win uplift point estimate >=+5 points with lower 95% bound >0, late survival misses do not increase, shed overflow falls or stays zero, and all strata pass non-inferiority. Revert if any repeated survival miss is attributable to admission, candidate invalid/no-op rate rises >0.5 points, terminal unsold value rises >2,000 median, or production win rate falls >5 points over 100 games.
confidence_and_status: High confidence in the mechanism and feasibility formulation; medium confidence in the proposed 48-turn horizon and 0.80/4-turn thresholds. Implementation: proposed. Benchmark: not run. Decision: experiment, not promote [uncertain].
computational_budget: Maintain incremental deadline buckets and route bounds in O(jobs+deadlines) per replan, target <20 ms and <5 MB extra memory. Replan after state changes or four times/day. If computation exceeds 100 ms, use a conservative cached demand table; on any exception/time pressure, fall back to a_v186 assignments while blocking all new development.
